name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
principle: A resource is initialized as one type but later interpreted or accessed as an incompatible type. The code may read invalid fields, corrupt object state, or in C/C++ access memory outside the real object layout.
detection_signals: C/C++ union member write followed by read of a different union member without matching discriminator update
C/C++ reinterpret_cast<T*> or C-style cast from one struct/class pointer type to an unrelated type
C/C++ void* stored with one concrete type and later cast to a different concrete type
C++ base pointer cast to derived type using static_cast or C-style cast without dynamic_cast check
Java cast from Object, Serializable, Map value, or collection element to a specific class without instanceof or Class::isInstance check
Type discriminator field such as type, kind, tag, msgType, opcode is not kept consistent with the active union/object field
PHP/Perl scalar operation or comparison on request/input value that can also be an array/reference
negative_signals: C++ std::variant access uses std::holds_alternative<T>() or std::get_if<T>() before std::get<T>()
C++ dynamic_cast<T*>(p) result is checked for null before dereference
Java code uses instanceof pattern matching or clazz.isInstance(x) before casting
C union access is guarded by an enum tag set in the same construction path as the active member
Deserialization or parsing code validates an explicit type tag against an allowlist before constructing/casting the object
Input parser rejects array syntax or non-scalar values before numeric/string scalar operations
false_defense_traps: Checking sizeof(target_type) but not proving the object was created as target_type
Trusting a user-controlled type/tag field to select the cast target
Using reinterpret_cast or C-style cast because the layouts appear identical
Catching ClassCastException after unsafe Java cast instead of preventing the bad type
Assuming union members are independent fields rather than aliases of the same storage
verification_focus: Can the same storage, pointer, object, or input value be created as one type and later used as another incompatible type on an attacker-influenced path?

consequence_chains.trigger: C/C++ wrong-type access uses a layout larger or different than the allocated object
consequence_chains.consequence: out-of-bounds read/write, crash, or code execution

consequence_chains.trigger: type confusion makes authorization logic take the default privileged branch

patch_principle: Keep a trusted discriminator/tag synchronized with the active union or object variant.
Replace raw unions and casts with type-safe variants, subclasses, or tagged structures.
Use dynamic_cast/instanceof/Class::isInstance/std::get_if before downcasts or variant access.
Validate parsed or request-supplied type information against an allowlist before casting or dispatch.
Reject unexpected scalar/array/reference types at trust boundaries.

minimal_examples.vuln: buf.msgType = NAME_TYPE; buf.nameID = attacker_int; printf("%s", buf.name);
minimal_examples.safe: buf.msgType = ID_TYPE; buf.nameID = id; printf("%d", buf.nameID);
